llmResponse.agendaChanges: The agenda items were handled in a compressed, informal study session format. Sections 1 (Call to Order / Roll Call), 2 (Welcome), 3 (Changes to Agenda), and 4 (Approval of Agenda) were all addressed very briefly and in rapid succession at the opening (approximately seconds 5–64). Section 5 (Information / Workforce Housing) dominated the session. Section 6 (Oral Communication) was conducted as public comment integrated into the Section 5 study session item rather than as a separate standalone segment. No formal resequencing was announced, but the procedural items were collapsed together without individual demarcation.

items.title: Welcome by the School Board President

publicComments.name: Chris R.
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about the legality of using Prop 39 bond funds for workforce housing under Article 13 of the California Constitution, questioned whether teachers actually want this type of housing, and suggested alternative funding mechanisms such as housing vouchers or a parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Elizabeth Starks
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for the community and teachers but emphasized the need to prioritize children's needs, asking where kids fit into the workforce housing plan and advocating for more community spaces and activities for youth.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: As leader of the classified staff union chapter, she strongly supported the housing project, emphasized the essential contributions of classified staff (paraeducators, custodians, food service, etc.), noted that rent increases have outpaced raises, and urged the board to move forward with housing that benefits all district employees.

publicComments.name: Hoover School Principal
publicComments.summary: As principal of Hoover Community School and a lifelong Redwood City resident, she expressed strong support for workforce housing, citing staff who live far away or with other families, and arguing that having staff live locally would rebuild community bonds.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker (visiting San Francisco school board member)
publicComments.summary: As a visiting San Francisco school board member interested in teacher housing, asked about the quality and durability of the building construction and how rental revenues are handled relative to bond repayment.

publicComments.name: Janet Góchez
publicComments.summary: As a district parent since 2008 who has seen two of her child's schools close partly due to teacher shortages driven by housing costs, she expressed strong support for workforce housing and also raised concerns about transportation challenges her child faces after being relocated to a new school.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: As president of the Redwood City Teachers Association, she confirmed that teachers do want this program, sharing examples of teachers whose lives improved with affordable housing, and personally expressed that even after 15+ years of teaching she cannot afford to buy locally, so reduced-rent housing could help her save for a down payment.
